1. 
Vide this award, I shall dispose off the statement of claim filed by the claimant/workman namely Sh.
Rohit Kumar against the management namely M/s Rajasthans Group.

Claim Of The Workman
Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023

1

2.
According to the claim of the workman, he was employed at the post of 'Peon' with the management since 21.06.2012.
He continuously worked at the same designation with the management till 04.06.2013 at his last drawn salary of Rs. 10,000/- per month.
Suddenly on 04.06.2013, the management illegally terminated his services without any cause or notice and without paying him his earned wages from January 2013 till June 2013.
2.1 Aggrieved of this action of the management, on 04.06.2013 workman sent a demand notice to it to which the management even replied but the grievance of the workman was not resolved.

Later,
the workman also approached the Labour Conciliation Officer also with his written grievance but no conciliation could take place there also.
After the conciliation proceedings failed, the present claim was filed before this court.
2.2 On the basis of the above averments in the claim, notice was issued to the management.
The AR of the management appeared and written statement was filed by the management.
REPLY OF THE MANAGEMENT 3.

In its reply, the management admitted that the workman was working with it since June 2012, but it took the defence that he was working as a Manager at the post of "Business Development Manager" at a monthly salary of Rs. 8,500/- per month besides facility of boarding, lodging and food being provided by the management.
The management alleged that while working with it, the workman embezzled huge amount of money from the funds of the management which he later admitted to and even repented for.
Taking a lenient view the management did not terminate the services of the workman but on 07.06.2013 the workman himself abandoned his duties and stopped reporting for his duties thereafter.
An FIR u/s 420 of IPC was registered against the workman for embezzling the funds of the management at Chandigarh.
ISSUES FRAMED 4.

After the rejoinder to the written statement was filed by the workman, on the basis of the pleadings the following issues were framed on 25.04.2014 :-
i) Whether the workman had started remaining absent from the duty illegally after embezzling the amount of Rs. 1,96,000/-?
OPM ii) Whether the workman had left the services of the management of his own on 07.06.2013 and had refused to come back on duty?
OPM iii) Whether the services of the workman had been terminated by the management illegally and/or unjustifiably?
OPW  iv) Relief.
After the issues were framed, the matter was then listed for workman's evidence.
Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183146019/
2
WORKMAN'S EVIDENCE 5.
The workman appeared in the witness box and filed his evidence by way of affidavit.
In this affidavit, the averments of the claim, as mentioned above were reiterated.

The workman relied upon the following documents:-
i) Ex. WW1/1 - Demand notice dated 04.06.2013 sent by him to the management.

ii) Ex. WW1/2 and Ex. WW1/3 - Postal receipts regarding sending of demand notice to the management.
iii) Ex. WW1/4 (OSR) - Reply cum notice of the management dated 12.06.2013 to the demand notice sent by the workman.
iv) Ex. WW1/5 - Statement of claim filed by workman before the conciliation officer.
v) Ex. WW1/6 - Failure report of conciliation officer.
5.1 The workman was cross-examined at length by the AR of the management.
5.2 Workman also examined Dr. Rati Singh, Conciliation Officer, North-West District, Labour Department as his witness to prove the conciliation proceedings.
He brought the record pertaining to file/ID No. 642/13/CO2/NWD which was exhibited as Ex. WW2/1.
He identified his signatures at several places on the conciliation proceedings.
This witness was also cross-examined by AR of the management.
5.3 No other witness was examined by AR for the workman and upon request, the evidence of the workman was closed and the matter was listed for management evidence.
MANAGEMENT'S EVIDENCE 6.
Sh. Junaid, Partner of the management appeared as the first witness of the management and filed his evidence by way of affidavit.
In this affidavit, the averments of the written statement were reiterated.

This witness relied upon the following documents:-
(i) Ex. MW1/1 (OSR) - Receipt dated 31.05.2013 issued by the workman.
(ii) Ex. MW1/2 (OSR) - Application form filled by the workman.
(iii) Ex. MW1/4 (OSR) - Letter written by the workman to the management.
(iv) Mark A - Copy of Complaint dated 07.06.2013 made by the management to SHO,
PS Neta Subhash Palace against the workman.

Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183146019/
3
(v) Mark B - Copy of FIR No. 248/14, P.S. Sec. 31, Chandigarh, lodged by one of the client of the management against the workman.
6.1 This witness was cross-examined at length by the AR of the workman.
6.2 Thereafter, Ct. Manoj Kumar, Delhi Police, appeared in the witness box as the summoned witness of the management.
He deposed that management filed a complaint registered at S. No. 791 against the workman in the police station at Subhash Place, Delhi.
He brought the original of the said complaint which was exhibited as Ex. MW2/2.
This witness was not cross-examined by the AR of the workman.

6.3 No other witness was examined by the management, so the evidence of the management was closed and the matter was then listed for final arguments.
ARGUMENTS 7.
The ARs of the both the parties advanced detailed arguments on 04.09.2023 which were heard by this court.
All the relevant documents on record were considered.
ISSUE-WISE FINDINGS 8.

The issue-wise findings on the basis of arguments advanced, written submissions filed, evidence led and all material on record are discussed in details in the sub-paragraphs that follows:-
Issue No.1 -: Whether the workman had started remaining absent from the duty illegally after embezzling the amount of Rs. 1,96,000/-?

OPM & Issue No.2 -:
Whether the workman had left the services of the management of his own on 07.06.2013 and had refused to come back on duty?

OPM 8.1 Both these issues being interconnected and essentially pertaining to the same aspect of 'Abandonment of Job'
by the workman shall be decided together.
8.2 The relationship of employer employee and the duration of employment is not in dispute in this case.
The management has admitted in its pleading that the workman was working with it from June 2012 and continued to work till June 2013.

The grievance of the claimant is that on 04.06.2013 his services were suddenly and unlawfully terminated by the management, while the defence taken by the management is that the workman embezzled the funds of the management while working with it and suddenly stopped reporting for his duties from 07.06.2013 willingly and without intimation.

8.3 The workman has placed on record the demand notice, Ex. WW1/1 and its proof of dispatch (postal receipts) Ex. WW1/2 & Ex. WW1/3 to establish that he had sent a demand notice to the management on 06.06.2013 seeking his reinstatement alongwith his already earned wages.

The address mentioned in this demand notice Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183146019/
4 was shown to the management witness Sh. Junaid, who is one of the Partners of the management and he admitted that the address mentioned in these documents was indeed the correct address of the management.
In such situation it can safely be presumed that a document sent through a post at the correct address of the management was indeed delivered to the management.
In his cross examination this witness evaded answering about the receipt of the delivery notice.
He stated and I quote from his cross-examination "I cannot say whether the management had received the demand notice or not."
This evasive response further lends weight to the averment of the claimant that the demand notice was duly delivered to the management.

Not only this, the workman has placed on record document Ex.
WW1/4, the reply of the demand notice as sent by the management through its advocate Anand & Associates which further proves the delivery of demand notice.
The workman relied upon this document in his chief examination and it was not put to him in cross examination that such a reply was never sent by the management.

In fact in the cross examination of the workman dated 04.03.2015 the counsel for the management referred to the reply to the demand notice, in a way admitting that the reply was sent by the management.
Thus, it is clear that the management had received the demand notice sent by the workman.

8.4 Further, the workman had admittedly also approached the Conciliation Officer with his grievance and the conciliation officer issued several notices to the management at its admittedly correct address to participate in the conciliation proceedings.

During trial, the conciliation officer appeared in the witness box as a witness of the workman and brought the entire record pertaining to the conciliation proceeding which he exhibited as Ex. WW2/1.
8.5

The act of the workman of sending a demand notice at the admittedly correct address of the management, approaching the Labour Conciliation Officer with his grievance and then agitating the matter and pursuing it before this court for around 10 years shows that he was and is keen on working with the management.
What other evidence can a worker lead to show that he was always keen on working but was not allowed to report for his duties by the management?
8.6 On the other hand the management, did not lead sufficient evidence to establish that the workman had himself abandoned his job.

The management could have placed on record the attendance record of the workman to show that while he continued to be reflected in the rolls of the management for a long time even after June 2013, but he did not come for his duties.
However, no such record was filed by the management.

The management did not place on record any document to show that when the workman, who had admittedly worked with the management for one year did not turn up for his duties, the management made any effort to contact him or conducted any enquiry against him, or in any manner issued a warning or direction to him to join back.

8.7 This conduct of the management of not placing on record any such document in support of its defence of 'abandonment' as taken by it further strengthens the case of the workman that he was unlawfully terminated.

Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183146019/
5 8.8

During the course of arguments, the Ld. AR for the management argued that the workman had cheated the management for around Rs. 2 lakhs and it was for this reason that he voluntarily stopped coming for his duties.
However throughout the trial, no evidence to show such embezzlement of funds/cheating by the workman was filed.
The management failed to establish any misconduct on the part of the claimant during his employment.

The receipts Ex. WW1/XMI1 (colly.)
do not in themselves show any embezzlement/cheating.
They at best only show that the claimant had issues these receipts.
How issuance of these receipts led to embezzlement/cheating has not been explained or established by the management.

The mere registration of an FIR (document Mark B)
against the workman is also grossly insufficient to establish any misconduct on his part.
This FIR was registered on 21.08.2014 i.e., around 9 years ago.
What was the outcome of the investigation in this FIR was never brought on record by the management.

Whether any evidence was led against the claimant in any court or whether the claimant was found guilty of any offence by a competent court was never brought on record by the management throughout the trial.

Thus, for want of evidence it cannot be said that the workman had a valid ground to abandon his job or indeed the workman had so acted that the management was justified in terminating his services without any enquiry.

8.9 Therefore, while the workman has been able to establish that he was unlawfully terminated, the management has failed to establish that the workman remained unauthorizedly absent from his duties after embezzling/cheating the management of some funds and he had refused to join his duties.
Thus, both these issues are decided in favour of the workman and against the management.
Issue No.3 -: Whether the services of the workman had been terminated by the management illegally and/or unjustifiably?
OPW 8.10
In view of the discussion above and the findings given in Issue Nos. 1 & 2 above, it is clear that the workman has established that he did not abandon his job.
In such scenario the onus was upon the management to show that it had followed the due prescribed process for retrenchment as provided under the Industrial Disputes Act.
The management admittedly did not give any retrenchment compensation, prior information, notice pay etc., to the claimant.
It also did not conduct any enquiry against the claimant following the principles of the natural justice.
It is thus clear that the services of the claimant were terminated illegally and or unjustifiably.
This issue is accordingly decided against the management and in favour of the workman.

8.11 Before parting with the findings on the issues it is important to discusses in brief yet another aspect on which even though no issue was framed by the Ld. Predecessor, the parties were at variance.

The management right from the written statement had taken the stand that the claimant was not a 'workman' but was appointed as a 'Business Development Manager' and therefore he does not fall under the category of 'workman' as defined u/s 2 (s) of the Industrial Disputes Act.

However no evidence was led by the management in support of its defence even in the face of clear averments and deposition by the claimant that he was working as a 'Peon' and not working in a 'Managerial'
capacity.
8.12 From the material placed on record during trial it only appears that the workman indeed was not performing any managerial function.

Signing payment receipts, collecting money or cheque from customers, depositing cheques or cash in the bank account cannot per se be said to be a work Rohit Kumar vs Rajasthans Group on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183146019/
6 can be done by a person only working in a managerial capacity.
Further, the admitted salary of the workman was only around Rs. 8,500/-.
Admittedly, the claimant was only class 10 th pass.

It was also admitted by the management witness in his cross- examination that he appointed the claimant without taking any document from him like his educational certificates, work experience certificate,
etc.

All these factors considered together and read with the un-rebutted testimony of the claimant that he was working as a 'Peon' indeed establish that he was employed as a 'workman' and there is nothing on record to hold that he was discharging any crucial 'management functions' or was employed as a 'manager'.
Relief :-
9. Coming now to the relief to which the workman is entitled.
Considering the facts of the case, this court is of the view that ends of justice would be met by granting lump sum compensation to the workman instead of reinstatement.

Thus, taking into account the short length of service of the workman of only one year, nature of his duties and his last drawn salary, I award a lump sum compensation of Rs. 40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand only) in favour of the workman and against the management which includes litigation expenses.
The management is directed to pay the said amount within a period of one month from the date of publication of this award.
In case of non- payment, interest @ 6% per annum from the date it becomes due, till the time it is realized, shall be paid by the management to the workman.

10. The attested copy of the award be sent to the Office of the Deputy Labour Commissioner,
Government of NCT of Delhi of Distt./Area concerned for publication, as per rules.
